chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
For everything there is a spring, and the spring of the Qur'an is the month of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: What is the spring of the Qur'an according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of 'spring' (Rabi') to describe Ramadan as the season of spiritual renewal for the Qur'an, reflecting the Shia tradition of viewing the month as a time when the Qur'an's meanings are revitalized in the hearts of believers. This concept underscores the unique status of Ramadan not merely as a period of fasting, but as the primary season for the Qur'an's active engagement and internalization. The narration aligns with the broader theological understanding that the Qur'an descends in its entirety during Laylat al-Qadr, making this month its temporal 'spring'.
